name: Violet-Blue (Crayola)
lede: Violet-Blue (Crayola) is a Crayola-branded name for a color our data finds is an exact match for the hue we file as [[violet-blue]].

sections.title: A crayon-box label
sections.body:
Our source for this name is Wikipedia's Crayola color list, which credits it to the Crayola crayon line without giving a release year [1]. In our own data, Violet-Blue (Crayola) and plain [[violet-blue]] are an exact match, 0.0 units apart, so the "(Crayola)" tag marks the brand, not a different color [2].

Its nearest distinct look-alike is [[soft-blue-violet]] (2.8 units, duller); [[gentian-blue]] and [[dark-periwinkle]] sit further off, at 5.4 and 5.8 [3].

In LCH terms it measures lightness 51, chroma 53 and hue 299 degrees, a blue-leaning violet rather than a true mid-point between the two hues [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That is unsurprising for a 20th-century crayon-box name this saturated, on top of an archive whose early centuries are thin to begin with [4].
